item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 181734
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Oct 18 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form well offshore of
southern Mexico during the next day or two. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression is likely to form around the middle of this
week while it moves westward to west-northwestward, well south of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 21a
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 181756
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 21A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1100 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026
 
...TRUDY PASSING SOUTHWEST OF CABO CORRIENTES...
...HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS IN PORTIONS OF SOUTHWEST AND
WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM MST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.3N 106.8W
ABOUT 105 MI...170 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 165 MI...265 KM W OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...974 MB...28.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Playa Perula to San Blas
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 12 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue to monitor the progress of Trudy.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM MST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 106.8 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A general northwestward 
motion is expected today, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest tonight. On the forecast track, the center of Trudy 
will move away from the coast of mainland Mexico this afternoon and 
then move south of Baja California Sur on Monday and Tuesday.
 
Reports from an Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft 
indicate that maximum sustained winds are now near 100 mph      
(155 km/h) with higher gusts.  Rapid weakening is expected to begin 
tonight, and Trudy could degenerate to a post-tropical low by 
Tuesday night.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The minimum central pressure estimated from the Hurricane Hunter 
aircraft data is 974 mb (28.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the mainland
Mexico portion of the Tropical Storm Warning area during the next
few hours, and in Las Islas Marias this afternoon.
 
RAINFALL: Through today, Trudy is expected to produce an additional
2 to 6 inches with isolated storm totals around 12 inches along and
near the southwest Mexican coast in Jalisco. This rainfall may
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce an additional
1 to 2 inches with isolated higher totals around 4 inches along the
southwest Mexican coast in northern Colima and southern Nayarit.
This rainfall may result in localized flash flooding, especially in
areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves
is likely in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico. These swells will cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 181434
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
800 AM MST Sun Oct 18 2026

Trudy has changed little in organization during the past few hours. 
The hurricane has a well-defined central dense overcast with cloud 
tops colder than -80C, and there have been occasional attempts at 
eye formation. The various subjective and objective satellite 
intensity estimates have an unusually large spread from 62-102 kt, 
but there has been little change in them since the previous 
advisory. Thus, the initial intensity is held at 90 kt.

The initial motion is still northwestward or 325/7 kt. This motion 
should continue today, followed by a turn toward the west-northwest 
at a slower forward speed as Trudy shears apart vertically and 
becomes steered by the lighter low- to mid-level flow. The new 
forecast track is similar to, but a little west of the previous 
track. On the forecast track, the hurricane will move away from 
southwest and west-central Mexico starting this afternoon and then 
move slowly south of Baja California Sur on Monday and Tuesday.

The hurricane is about to encounter increasing southwesterly shear 
and a drier and more stable airmass. The dynamical intensity 
guidance forecasts this combination to cause rapid weakening 
beginning just after 12 h, and the intensity forecast follows the 
trend of this guidance. The new forecast follows the previous 
forecast, showing Trudy degenerating to a post-tropical cyclone by 
60 hours and dissipating in 3 or 4 days. And as mentioned 
previously, both of these could occur sooner than currently 
predicted.


KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions are expected in the tropical storm 
warning area today.
 
2. A dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves is likely
in areas of onshore winds within the warning areas.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will continue to impact the 
southwest Mexican coast between Colima and Nayarit through today. 
This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will continue to affect the coast of southwestern
Mexico and west-central Mexico during the next few days, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
